_meta.indication: TRULICITY is indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
_meta.receipt_date: September 18, 2014 (BLA dated September 17, 2014, received September 18, 2014); original BLA submitted September 18, 2013

pivotal_trials.trial_name: H9X-MC-GBCF (Stage II), dulaglutide as add-on to metformin
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, parallel-group, double-blind, placebo-controlled, active-controlled, adaptive dose finding (R, PG, DB, PC, AC, ADF)
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes on background metformin, compared dulaglutide 0.75 mg and 1.5 mg weekly to placebo (26 weeks) and to sitagliptin 100 mg (52 weeks)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in HbA1c from baseline to the landmark visit (week 26 vs placebo; week 52 vs sitagliptin)
pivotal_trials.n: Dula 0.75 mg-281, Dula 1.5 mg-279, Sitagliptin-273, Pbo/sitagliptin-139

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, parallel-arm, active-controlled, double-blind, double-dummy comparing dulaglutide to metformin in T2DM
pivotal_trials.population: Patients at least 18 years old with 6.5% ≤ HbA1c ≤ 9.5% and BMI 23-45 kg/m2; dulaglutide used as monotherapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 26
pivotal_trials.result: HbA1c reduction vs metformin (wk 26): Dula 0.75 mg -0.15 (95% CI -0.29, -0.01), Dula 1.5 mg -0.22 (95% CI -0.36, -0.08)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%): nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and decreased appetite; e.g., nausea 12.4% (0.75 mg) and 21.1% (1.5 mg) vs 5.3% placebo; vomiting 6.0% and 12.7% vs 2.3% placebo.
target_moa: Dulaglutide is a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist that binds and activates the GLP-1 receptor, augmenting glucose-stimulated insulin secretion, inhibiting glucagon release, and delaying gastric emptying.
modality: Fusion protein (GLP-1 variant linked to Fc portion of human IgG4); a peptide-Fc fusion / GLP-1 receptor agonist biologic

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: RISK OF THYROID C-CELL TUMORS — dulaglutide causes a dose-related and treatment-duration-dependent increase in thyroid C-cell tumors (adenomas and carcinomas) in rats; human relevance unknown; contraindicated in patients with personal/family history of MTC or MEN 2.

rems.type: A REMS consisting of a communication plan was required to ensure the benefits outweigh the potential risk of medullary thyroid carcinoma and the risk of pancreatitis.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; no new efficacy or safety issue rose to the level of requiring advisory panel input.

citations.quote: - Updates to the prescribing information (PI) to add information on the use of Trulicity in patients taking basal insulin, based on the Phase 3 study H9X-MC-GBDI (AWARD 9) - A Randomized, Double- Blind Trial Comparing the Effect of Dulaglutide 1.5 mg with Placebo on Glycemic Control in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes on Basal Insulin Glargine;

description.text: Added efficacy and safety data for dulaglutide in type 2 diabetes patients with moderate or severe chronic kidney disease (AWARD-7)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application proposes to add efficacy and safety information to the prescribing information based on the clinical data from the Phase 3 study H9X-MC-GBDX (AWARD 7) – A Randomized, Open-Label, Parallel-Arm Study Comparing the Effect of Once-Weekly Dulaglutide with Insulin Glargine on Glycemic Control in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes and Moderate or Severe Chronic Kidney Disease.

description.text: Added efficacy and safety data for Trulicity in combination with an SGLT2 inhibitor (with or without metformin) in type 2 diabetes mellitus

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for the following changes for Trulicity (dulaglutide) injection: the addition of efficacy and safety information to the Prescribing Information on the use of Trulicity in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) patients based on the clinical data from the Phase 3 Study GBGE (AWARD-10), a 24-week, Phase 3b, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-arm, multicenter trial that investigated the effects of the addition of once-weekly dulaglutide 1.5 mg or 0.75 mg to an SGLT2 inhibitor, with or without concomitant use of metformin, on glycemic control and safety in patients with inadequately controlled T2DM.

description.text: Added new indication for reduction of major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for the addition of efficacy and safety information to the Prescribing Information, including a new indication for reduction of major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus, based on the clinical data from Study GBDJ (REWIND), a Phase 3 cardiovascular outcomes trial.

description.text: Added higher doses of 3.0 mg and 4.5 mg once weekly as adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for the use of additional doses of Trulicity, 3.0 mg and 4.5 mg once weekly, as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

description.text: Expanded indication to include pediatric patients 10 years of age and older with type 2 diabetes mellitus

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sBLA provides for expansion of the indication for Trulicity, as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control, to pediatric patients 10 years of age and older with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

summary.text: Trulicity (dulaglutide) was approved via a standard BLA under section 351(a) of the PHS Act for improving glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes, supported by five phase 3 trials; approval included a boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors and a REMS communication plan, with no advisory committee convened and required postmarketing studies including a cardiovascular outcomes trial.

citations.quote: On September 18, 2013 Eli Lilly and Company submitted a Biologics License Application (BLA) for Trulicity under section 351 of the Public Health Service Act.
